outcomes.text: Recognise, analyse and use the accidence and syntax listed in the language appendix.
Extend vocabulary and knowledge of linguistic structures through wider reading and study of Latin passages.
Translate an unseen passage of Livy narrative prose accurately into English.
Translate an unseen passage of Ovid verse accurately into English.
Show detailed understanding of the structure of individual words, phrases and sentences in ancient authors.
Scan two lines of unseen Latin verse accurately.
Present information clearly, concisely and logically using correct English terminology.
Recognise, analyse and use the accidence and syntax from the language appendix, as the task needs.
Build vocabulary and linguistic knowledge by studying Latin passages and reading widely.
Translate unseen English material accurately into Latin.
Show detailed understanding of how ancient authors build words, phrases and sentences.
Show understanding of an unseen Latin prose passage through comprehension questions.
Translate part of the passage and answer questions on its syntax and accidence.
Present answers clearly and coherently using suitable English terminology.
Study one Group 1 and one Group 2 prose set text for the examined series.
Show detailed knowledge and understanding of the prose set texts studied.
Understand and respond to passages taken from a set text.
Translate passages of each set text into English.
Read a selection of ancient literature in English translation to understand where the set texts come from.
Show knowledge of the wider context of a set text.
Understand the social, cultural and historical contexts of the texts, their authors and audiences.
Use appropriate historical or cultural knowledge to explain a given phrase, sentence or passage.
Identify, analyse and evaluate literary techniques, characterisation, strength of argument and meaning in set texts.
Use correct technical terms in English to describe literary features of the texts.
Critically analyse the style, characterisation, argument and meaning of a set passage.

subtopics.title: Writing at length on prose texts

outcomes.text: Select relevant material from texts studied to support an argument and summarise findings.
Write at length using both the set text and material studied in translation.
Present information clearly and coherently in extended English writing.
Study one Group 3 and one Group 4 verse set text for the examined series.
Show detailed knowledge of the verse set texts studied, including metre.
Understand and respond to passages taken from a set text.
Translate passages of each set text into English.
Read a selection of ancient literature in English translation to understand where the set texts come from.
Show knowledge of the wider context of a set text.
Understand the social, cultural and historical contexts of the texts, their authors and audiences.
Use appropriate historical or cultural knowledge to explain a given phrase, sentence or passage.
Identify, analyse and evaluate literary techniques, characterisation, argument and meaning in verse set texts.
Use correct technical terms in English to describe literary features of the texts.
Critically analyse the style, characterisation, argument and meaning of a set passage.

subtopics.title: Writing at length on verse texts

outcomes.text: Select relevant material from texts studied to support an argument and summarise findings.
Write at length using both the set text and material studied in translation.
Present information clearly and coherently in extended English writing.
Use nouns of all standard types, plus bos, domus, Iuppiter and vis.
Use adjectives of all three declensions, including dives, pauper and vetus.
Form and use adverbs.
Form comparatives and superlatives of adjectives and adverbs.
Recognise pronouns, pronominal adjectives and related forms.
Use verbs of all conjugations in all moods, voices and tenses.
Use deponent, semi-deponent, defective, irregular and impersonal verbs, including the impersonal passive.
Form compound verbs with common prefixes, including their consonant and vowel changes.
Use cardinal numbers 1-1000 and ordinal numbers 1st-10th.
Use prepositions correctly.
Apply standard patterns of case usage.
Express negation.
Form direct statements, questions (including deliberative) and commands.
Express prohibitions, exhortations and wishes.
Use the infinitive as subject, complement, prolative and historic.
Use participles, including the ablative absolute.
Use the subjunctive in potential and generic senses.
Express comparison, including the ablative of comparison.
Use the gerund and gerundive, including the gerundive of obligation.
Use constructions with quominus and quin.
Use dum and dummodo to mean 'provided that'.
Form indirect statement, including extended oratio obliqua, plus indirect question, command and prohibition.
Form descriptive relative clauses, including common subjunctive uses.
Form subordinate clauses within indirect speech.
Express purpose, including uses of the gerund and gerundive.
Express result, including the comparative with quam ut.
Form conditional clauses.
Form causal clauses.
Form temporal clauses.
Express fearing, prevention and precaution.
Form concessive clauses.
Form comparative clauses.
